newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-AUSTRALIAN GRAY HEADS FOR FIRST TITLE IN PGA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-AUSTRALIAN GRAY HEADS FOR FIRST TITLE IN PGA.

text.p: Australian golfer Chris Gray fired
a third round of six-under-par 66 on Saturday to set himself on
course for his first professional title in the Australian PGA
championship.
Gray's round, the best of the day, saw him open up a lead of
six shots with an aggregate of 12-under 204 going into Sunday's
final round of the A$400,000 (US$316,000) tournament at the New
South Wales golf course.
Gray, 28, held a similar lead in a minor tournament in
Western Australia two years ago, only to shoot a disappointing
final round of 74 and lose.
"I have waited six years and I feel like it's my time, like
I'm ready to win," Gray, who won the 1990 Australian amateur
title, told reporters.
Gray leads from Jerry Kelly of the United States and fellow
Australian Peter Lonard. Kelly carded a 71 while Lonard, whose
career was in doubt two years ago through illness, hit a 72.
Anthony Painter and Justin Cooper, both from Australia, were
a further shot back on 211.
Gray's putter was the mainstay of a round which included six
birdies between the fourth and 11th holes. He sank long putts of
over 10 yards for birdies at the 11th and 14th holes.
European Tour regular Wayne Riley of Australia dropped out
of contention with a 76, including a triple bogey six at the
15th hole, to be among nine players grouped on 215.
